faqs.a: A slug is the readable part of a URL, like the-10-best-tea-brands in example.com/blog/the-10-best-tea-brands. It tells both users and search engines what the page is about.
Hyphens are the standard choice and the one Google recommends as word separators. Underscores work, but Google treats them as joiners (red_apple can read as redapple), so hyphens are safer for SEO.
faqs.q: Should I use hyphens or underscores?

faqs.a: Keep slugs under about 60 characters. Shorter URLs rank no better directly, but they get clicked and shared more often, and they never get cut off in social previews.
faqs.q: How long should a slug be?

faqs.a: Yes. Accented characters (é, ü, ñ) are transliterated to plain ASCII (e, u, n) using Unicode normalization, and non-Latin characters are removed so the URL always works everywhere.
Stop words are common words (the, and, of, in) that add little meaning. Removing them shortens the slug, but keeping them keeps the slug more readable — it is a style choice, not an SEO requirement.
faqs.q: Should I remove stop words from my slug?

url-slug-generator.formula:
1. NFD-normalize, strip combining marks; transliterate ß->ss, æ->ae, œ->oe, ø->o, ł->l, ñ->n ...
2. If lowercase on: whole string -> toLowerCase()
3. Remove everything except a-z A-Z 0-9 space hyphen
4. Split on whitespace/hyphens; optionally drop stop words (the, a, an, and, or, of, in, on, ...)
5. Join words with - (or _)
6. If longer than max length: cut to max length, then trim back to the last separator (min 10 chars kept)
howTo: Paste or type your page title into the title box.
Choose the separator: hyphen (-) is the SEO standard; underscore (_) is an option.
Toggle Force lowercase on (recommended) and stop-word removal as you like.
Adjust Max length — 60 characters is a good default.
Copy the generated slug, or download it as a .txt file.
Check the preview URL to see how it will look live.
keyFacts: A URL slug is the human-readable tail of a URL: example.com/blog/your-slug-here.
Hyphens are the recommended word separator; underscores are treated as word joiners by Google.
Accented letters are transliterated to ASCII (é -> e, ü -> u, ñ -> n) so links never break.
Stop words (the, and, of, in) can be stripped to shorten the slug.
Slugs are truncated at the max length on a word boundary, never mid-word.
This generator runs 100% in your browser — no data leaves your device.

limitations: Stop-word removal uses an English stop-word list only; it does not apply to Hindi or Arabic titles.
Non-Latin scripts (Devanagari, Arabic, Chinese) are removed from slugs, not transliterated — a title in those scripts produces an empty slug.
Transliteration covers common Latin accents; rare characters may fall back to being removed.
The max-length trim keeps at least 10 characters before cutting at the last separator, so very short titles stay intact.
